Obviously, we're back doing our meetings virtually because of the rise in cases and as a result of the significant increase in cases on both Saturday and Sunday. The Clerk, CAO, and I had a conversation and determined it best that we revert back to a virtual meeting. You know, we didn't want to be here, but we really enjoyed being back, seeing all of you in person in the chambers. But we thought it was important, not just from a safety perspective, but also to emphasize to the community at large that we are, again, in a challenging situation and we all have to take the public health precautions that a woman public health is urging us to take. I would draw to everybody's attention that Algoma Public Health issued orders today and those orders relate to a number of aspects of COVID-19. Specifically, it will be legally ordering anyone in Algoma who has confirmed or suspected COVID-19 infection, that is confirmed or suspected, or who is identified as a close contact. So either you have COVID-19, you're suspected to have COVID-19, or you're identified as a close contact. You will have to follow isolation requirements. And if you do not follow isolation requirements, it will be a legal offense and fines can follow that. Algoma Public Health is also requiring subsidiary businesses and organizations to reinstate the recently lifted provincial capacity limits. So people should expect to adjust their attendances at places. For instance, the Memorial Gardens, as capacity will be rolled back to 50%, as opposed to full capacity. And we'll work with our community partners to ensure that we do that properly. It's also important to recognize that you need to be masked indoors and outdoors when you're in a situation where you can't be more than two meters from another party that you do not live with. And you will need proof of vaccination and proof of ID if you're over 12 years old, if you're entering any indoor facility or actively participating as a coach, an official volunteer or spectator at an organized sporting event. So there are a number of restrictions and requirements in place that will come into place this week as a result of our significant increase in COVID-19 cases here in Sault Ste. Marie. And I encourage all residents to learn about those and follow them. Algoma Public Health's release had some interesting information that I want to make sure I share with the community so that we all have it. On Sunday, November 14th, 2021, Algoma Public Health reached a milestone of over 709 cases of COVID-19 reported since the outset of the pandemic. COVID-19 activity in Algoma is rising and it's currently the highest that it had ever been since the beginning of the pandemic. Algoma's rate of new COVID-19 cases is among the highest in Ontario at this time. As of November 14th, there are 155 active cases in Algoma with 14 hospitalizations. In the seven day period from November 8th to November 14th, rates of new COVID-19 cases in Algoma were at 121.5 cases per 100,000 population and rising with the most recent percent positivity of 4%. By comparison, in early October, the seven day incident was less than five cases per 100,000 and the percent positivity was less than 0.5%. So we've gone from less than five cases per 100,000 to 121.5 cases per 100,000 in less than a half a percent positivity rate to a 4% positivity rate. We've gone from having one of the lowest prevalences of COVID-19 in the province of Ontario to having one of the highest. So we have to all be very sensitive to the fact that this virus is still in our community and it is evidently spreading rapidly. People who are not fully immunized are at a higher risk of COVID-19 infection. Since the beginning of Algoma's fourth wave of the pandemic in early July, 64% of COVID-19 cases were people who are not fully immunized. Fully immunized people can still get sick from COVID-19 and spread the infection. Since the beginning of Algoma's fourth wave of the pandemic in early July, 36% of COVID-19 cases were in people who were fully immunized. So it's important that if you have any symptoms, however mild they may be, whether you are vaccinated, are unvaccinated or unvaccinated that you stay home and you get tested. If you have children, it's important that you screen your children using the province's screening tool before they go to school or before they go to daycare. I believe very deeply in this community and we have demonstrated throughout this pandemic that when we act collectively and we can act collectively, we can get our numbers down and keep them down. So I will encourage you to familiarize yourself with Algoma Public Health's advice, follow it, encourage your family and friends to follow it. For those of you who have your first dose, get your second dose as soon as you can. For those of you who can get a booster dose, make your appointment to get your booster dose. And for those of you who do not have either doses, please familiarize yourself with the vaccination process and speak to medical experts who can give you proper information upon which you can make your decision. So I encourage everybody to be sensitive and careful as they kind of engage with each other over the coming intervening timeframe. We are at significant risk to see COVID continue to increase in our community and we need to work together to make sure that we can slow its spread. I have confidence that we can and that we will.
